prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there’s no single “best” roofer for everyone — the best one for you depends on your neighborhood, roof type, insurance situation, and whether you want the lowest price, fastest turn‑around, or the strongest warranty. Instead of naming one company, here’s a practical way to find the best hail‑damage roofer in Denver and the exact things to verify.

If you want direct local names, tell me your ZIP code and whether the job is residential or commercial and I’ll give a short list of highly rated local contractors and a recommended pick‑order.

How to find the best roofer for hail damage
- Get at least 3 written estimates for the same scope of work.
- Prefer local, established companies (not “storm chasers”) with a permanent office and local references.
- Check reviews on Google, BBB, Angi/HomeAdvisor, Yelp and Nextdoor. Call recent customers for references.
- Verify insurance and licensing:
  - Ask for their CO business license/registration and local Denver business address.
  - Confirm general liability and workers’ compensation — get the insurer and policy numbers and call to verify.
- Manufacturer certifications matter: look for GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Platinum/Preferred, or similar. These affect warranty options.
- Experience with insurance claims: hail work is insurance‑driven. Use a roofer familiar with adjusters and scope/line‑item documentation, but beware contractors who tell you to lie to your insurer or pressure you into switching your claim.

Questions to ask every roofer
- How long have you been in business in Denver? (Local tenure matters.)
- Do you pull permits and handle inspections? (They should.)
- Will you provide a written, itemized estimate and a sample contract? (Yes.)
- Do you provide a workmanship warranty and a manufacturer shingle warranty? Explain the terms.
- Who will be on the job each day? Are subcontractors used? Are they insured?
- Do you provide lien releases and final paperwork?
- Can you provide at least 3 recent local references for hail damage repairs?

Red flags
- Pressure to sign immediately or demand large cash payments up front.
- No local address, only a P.O. box, or recent online-only presence after a big storm.
- Refusal to pull permits or to provide proof of insurance.
- Very low bid compared to others with vague scope or “we’ll do whatever adjuster wants” answers.

Insurance and payment tips
- Get the scope in writing and match all estimates to the same scope so bids are comparable.
- Never sign a full release until the job is complete and final payment is made and you have lien waivers.
- Ask whether they will bill the insurer directly and what they’ll charge for upgrades the insurer won’t cover.

If you’d like:
- Give me your ZIP code and I’ll list 3–5 well‑reviewed Denver roofers (I can’t browse right now, but I can suggest likely types of reputable contractors and how to rank them).
- I can draft an email/phone script or a comparison table to send to contractors.
Which would you prefer?
